newsitem.title: RUSSIA: AGROKHLEB-Russia's 1997 winter wheat crop may slip.
newsitem.headline: AGROKHLEB-Russia's 1997 winter wheat crop may slip.

text.p: The following is a direct contribution from the Agrokhleb Report, published by SovEcon Ltd, an independent research organisation specialising in agricultural production and trade in the former Soviet Union.
RUSSIA 97 WINTER WHEAT OUTPUT SEEN DOWN DESPITE GOOD SNOW COVER

MOSCOW, Feb 21 - Russia's total winter wheat output is provisionally forecast at 16.7 million tonnes -- or in a range between 16.0-17.5 million tonnes -- compared with a winter crop of 17.1 million in 1996.
The failure of the autumn sowing campaign will more than compensate for the fact that growing conditions are generally good and yields in most areas on the rise.
Due to a mild winter and good snow cover, winter-kill losses in 1997 are expected to decline to about 0.5 million hectares, as against 0.8 million hectares in 1996.
It will account for only six percent of winter wheat acreage sown for the 1997 harvest, compared with nine percent last year.
The expected decline in winter-kill losses mainly reflects better conditions in the North Caucasus -- the major winter wheat producing area.
It particularly concerns the Rostov area, which seriously suffered from adverse weather conditions last year.

Assuming a normal crop development, winter wheat yields are anticipated to increase in most areas, particularly in the North Caucasus, where winter wheat output may increase to 8.8 million tonnes, about 1.0 million tonnes up on last year.
